utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I notice that General Miletic is back. General Beara isn't present today. Mr. Ostojic, the information that we have is that he is not feeling well. Will we have the waiver within the day?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Ms. Fauveau, in relation to yesterday's absence of your client, I don't recall having seen the waiver as yet -- oh, it has arrived now. All right. Okay. Thank you. Now, Prosecution today is represented by Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. I think that comes to Defence teams, we have a full house today. The witness is already present, so we can start with his testimony. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I would just like to introduce our new member of our team. It is Ms. Antigoni Xagoraraki.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, ma'am, and welcome. So you finished with your cross-examination, Mr. Zivanovic, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, yesterday you said you would need about 15 minutes or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We have no questions for this witness at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Ms. Nikolic, go ahead and introduce yourself to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in the courtroom. Good morning, Mr. Trisic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Although we've already met, I am going to introduce myself for the record. My name is Jelena Nikolic, and I represent, together with Mr. Bourgon, Mr. Drago Nikolic. I am going to put several questions to you on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yesterday during your testimony, on pages 27030 and 27031, you testified that during the period of 1992 within the 5th Battalion of the Birac Brigade you were in charge of security and intelligence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, during the war you were in charge of those tasks only for those two months?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. Only for the two months that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And after the months of September and October 1992, you were assigned to completely different tasks in the logistics part of the brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: While you were in charge of the intelligence and security detail, were you familiar with the documents of the JNA such as the command of the work of the commands and staffs and the rules of service of security service, the military police, the instruction on the methods of work of the security service, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially, not completely.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the methods of work in counter-intelligence and the application of these methods?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not completely.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that in the course of your work in the security organ, you knew about the work of this organ only as much as was going on within the framework of your brigade; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And you did not have any other experience with regard to the work of the security organs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. I did not have any other experience.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when we met a few days ago that you told me that you had not read the rules of the work of the security organ, that you did not deal with that because you were keen to leave that kind of duty as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The job did not suit me at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to move on and put several questions to you about something else. Yesterday, on pages 27062 and 27063, you testified about your presence at a meeting, the meeting took place on the 12th of July, 1995, at the command of the Bratunac Brigade. Do you remember that? I apologise, my mistake. That you were actually a member of the Bratunac Brigade when a meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And in the course of that day, at the brigade command you saw officers from various -- other units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Since you hail from Bratunac or the general region of Bratunac, did you personally know Drago Nikolic from the Zvornik Brigade? Did you know what he looked like?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had met and I knew what he looked like.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: During those days and on that day, did you see Mr. Drago Nikolic in the Bratunac Brigade from the Zvornik Brigade, or did you see any other officer from the Zvornik Brigade for that matter?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see Drago Nikolic. I did not meet him around that time. I don't know about any others.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In addition to that, on page 27069 yesterday, you mentioned on line 10 that in Potocari on the 12th of July, 1995, you had seen, amongst others, members of the Zvornik Brigade. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to those people? Did they introduce themselves to you? Did they tell you what unit they were from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't talk to them, and obviously, they did not introduce themselves to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: So how did you conclude that they were from the Zvornik Brigade, based on what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, members of the Zvornik Brigade wore patches on the sleeves depicting the words, "The Army of Republika Srpska" with the insignia of the Zvornik Brigade wolves or something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Trisic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Nikolic. Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have 15 minutes of question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I am Natacha Ivanovic. I represent General Miletic. I would like to ask you a few questions on a precise subject which has to do with fuel which the Bratunac Brigade received in July 1995. I would like you to see document 4D613. Could we please see page 3 of the document in B/C/S because I think the English version is page 2. Excuse me, it's page 2 in B/C/S and page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear in it the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You spoke yesterday about 30.000 litres which the Bratunac Brigade had received from the DutchBat, page 56 of yesterday's notes. And you said yesterday, also on page 56, that these 30.000 litres, which appear here at item 2, UNHCR. Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I'd like to clarify a point. Why do you say it was received from the DutchBat, this fuel? It says here that it is UNHCR which is indicated on this document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My associate, the assistant for traffic, indicated that. That's what he wrote. I was present when this fuel was unloaded from the tank of the Dutch battalion into the tank of the Vihor transport company.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: All right. I will come back on this point a little bit later. Do you remember when this fuel was received? Do you remember the date for these 30.000 litres, when they were received?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, this could have been on the 13th. Most probably on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown 5D1385. Is this document a receipt for the fuel, the 30.000 litres which the Bratunac Brigade received?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Just to be quite clear, where you can read "7042 Bratunac," is it indeed the number of the military post of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The date on this document is indeed the 13th of July, as you indicated a while ago.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like now to see 1386, document 1386. 5D1386, please. Is this document a receipt by the Vihor society -- company of part of this fuel which would be part of 30.000 litres which was, before that, received by the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it says 23.300. That's what he it says here, 23.300. You would have to jog my memory a little.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: If I can help you, the date on this document is the 14th of July, 1995, and one can read at the top "Military post 7402" and between brackets "UNHCR," between brackets.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is probably a document that we issued to Vihor which means that we took over the fuel and transferred it on to Vihor, and this is the document proving that the fuel ended up with Vihor and that they owe us that fuel.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This document just as the one you spoke about a little while ago, also indicates UNHCR, doesn't it? Now, what I would like to know is that you said you were present in the DutchBat bases when the fuel was being given to the authorities of the Republika Srpska, but this fuel indeed was at the DutchBat, but you don't know whether the owner could have been the HCR, UNHCR?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you misspoke. The fuel was unloaded from the tank of the DutchBat within the perimeter of the Vihor company, into their tank, and I was present when this was done. From the tank of the DutchBat into the Vihor tank. I really can't tell you after such a long time why that was the case. I suppose that it was customary for the UNHCR forces, at least that's what my associate wrote. And in confirmation that the fuel indeed was secured by DutchBat, there was a conversation between General Mladic and the commander of the DutchBat at the Fontana Hotel in Bratunac, and listening to that conversation, you can see and hear that the commander of the DutchBat promises to deliver fuel for the transport of Muslims to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: All right. Precisely speaking about the transport of the Muslims to Tuzla, you said yesterday at page 56 that the fuel received was in order to transport the Muslim population from Bratunac to Tuzla. Is it true that on the 13th of July, 1995, part of the Muslim population was still in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be more accurate to say that indeed this fuel had been received to transport the Muslim population from Potocari to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We saw on the receipt of the Bratunac Brigade that the fuel was received on the 13th of July, 1995. The fuel was received while the transport was in progress?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true to say that at the time there was a dearth of fuel in the Republika Srpska? Maybe there is a translation problem. Is it true that at the time in July 1995 there wasn't enough fuel in the Republika Srpska? I'm being told --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am only following in English, and in English I am receiving the translation of what you are saying in French. But you have to help me and tell me whether -- those who are following in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apparently there is a problem because the witness doesn't receive the translation in his language, so maybe there is a technical problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That I understood, but what I wanted to know is whether -- if he is the only one who is not receiving translation or whether there are others such as the accused? You are receiving translation. So the problem seems to be with the witness and not with others, as far as I can see. I see Mr. Nikolic nodding as well. Are you receiving interpretation now of what I am saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I can hear you but I did not see the lady -- actually, I did not hear the interpretation of her words whereas I hear the interpretation of yours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So then it's not a technical problem on his side, it's -- we need to check again with the booth that is translating from French into B/C/S. And I would kindly ask Madam Fauveau to repeat her question. You have it on the transcript, but if you would need my assistance I will of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true, witness, that at the time in July 1995, there was a dearth of fuel in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can it be said that without the help -- can we say that without the help of the international organisations, those 30.000 litres of fuel, it wouldn't have been possible to transport the Muslim population at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that. But in any case, it made the transport easier for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You're absolutely sure that this fuel had been received precisely for the transport of the Muslim population of Potocari towards the territory controlled by the -- of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That question has been asked and clearly answered, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would answer exactly what my colleague has said. I am now cross-examining, that's what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed. We are losing and wasting more time like that, Mr. Thayer. Please, if witness could answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you wish me to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Are you absolutely certain that those 30.000 litres of fuel were received for the need to transport the Muslim population from Potocari towards the territory which was under the control of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no other question to ask from you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Fauveau. [In English] Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Trisic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I am Drago Krgovic, and I am going to put some questions to you in relation to your testimony. Mr. Trisic, in response to my colleague Mr. Lazarevic's question yesterday, you mentioned at a certain point that a forward command post of the Drina Corps was established in the Pribicevac sector. Do you recall saying that to my colleague Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You testified before this Tribunal in the Blagojevic case, transcript page from 19344 on, and on that occasion you described your stay at Pribicevac in July 1995. Do you recall testifying about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trisic, who did you go to Pribicevac at that time in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Pribicevac with Mr. Davidovic, my friend, and the then president of the executive board of the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This was on the 9th of July, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you came to Pribicevac, where did you go first? The logistics base was there as well, of the Bratunac Brigade or, rather, of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we came to Pribicevac, we first stopped off at the rear section -- sector of the 3rd Battalion that was located at Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you stayed there, as you said in the Blagojevic case, for an hour, two hours at the most?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stayed approximately for that long at Pribicevac, an hour or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that at one point in time while you were there in the rear logistics base, General Gvero arrived also at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trisic, can you please tell us if he was escorted by anybody or accompanied by anyone? How did he come? With which vehicle, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. It was a little bit unusual to me. He arrived in a private car with only a driver, and this was a bit unusual, as far as I was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to speak with General Gvero then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. We sat together at a table. We were drinking coffee and a drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did General Gvero tell you that he came to oversee the Srebrenica operation, to propose some measures or to have any kind of activity, or did you talk about everyday things?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We mostly talked about everyday things. It was a little bit unusual, as far as I was concerned, because he didn't -- or, there wasn't much talk about the Srebrenica operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did General Gvero ask you to submit a report or anything like that to him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And did you leave that place to go to the front line or did you spend the whole time there at that table, as you described earlier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in one place the whole time and that's where this conversation took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when did you return to Bratunac? Did General Gvero leave at the same time or did he stay at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After our conversation, Davidovic and I started back, and at the same time, but in a separate vehicle, Mr. Gvero left too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the type of the vehicle in which General Gvero arrived?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't say now. It was a long time ago. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did any of the Drina Corps senior officers stay at Pribicevac at that time? Were any of them at Pribicevac at that time when you were there, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. I really couldn't say, probably there were some there, but anything that I would try to say would be just speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see General Gvero suggesting any measures to General Krstic, make any suggestions or ask him to take any steps or actions or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Nothing like that happened. I didn't see that. Like I said, it was just an ordinary everyday conversation, so this was a bit of a surprise to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trisic, thank you very much. I have no further questions. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just a few questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Trisic, my name is Peter Haynes and I represent Vinko Pandurevic, who at the time you were talking about was the commander of the Zvornik Brigade. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand the question. Do I remember ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That in 1995, July of 1995, Vinko Pandurevic was the commander of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask you -- to follow on from some questions Madam Nikolic asked you about the soldiers you saw in Potocari with the insignia on their arms. How many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't give you a number. In any case, it was probably just a small number of soldiers. It was a small room and it couldn't hold a large number of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And in terms of their dress, they were wearing ordinary camouflage uniforms, and what struck you was the wolf insignia upon their arms; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if you can't answer this, then you mustn't, but are we talking about one or two or -- as small a number as that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Very well. I wonder if you could just look at something for me. Could we have in e-court, please, 7D63 and page 6. Do you recognise the insignia you saw on these few soldiers' arms on that sheet of paper, and if so, can you indicate which one it was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I cannot recognise any.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So it comes to this, all you can recall is seeing a few soldiers who had a wolf insignia on their arm; is that it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, for this next series of questions, Mr. President, I think we had better go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that, let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The English is C, the B/C/S is B. Now, Mr. Trisic, you -- let me explain what this document is because you won't have seen it before, I don't think. The army of Bosnia and Herzegovina apparently had the ability to intercept military communications between units of the army of Republika Srpska, and they recorded them and wrote them down. And what you have on the right-hand side of your screen, in fact you may only have the Serbian version, is what was written down of a conversation they apparently intercepted, and the conversation is between you and somebody called Obrenovic on the 13th of July, at about 20 to 7.00 in the evening. Do you know who Major Dragan Obrenovic was in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you know that at that time, at about quarter to 7.00 in the evening of the 13th of July, he was in command of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's a long time ago, but do you remember talking to him, on the evening of the 13th of July, about a broken down tank?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that conversation, but it's possible; and based on this text, it's possible that we did have such a conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So, if you don't recall the conversation, there is little point in my asking you anymore about it; but reading this, does it refresh your memory about the conversation you had with Dragan Obrenovic shortly before 7.00 on the evening of the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could have had such a conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much, Mr. Trisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to you, to Your Honours. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My name is Nelson Thayer, and I will be asking you some questions on behalf of the Prosecution. If my voice gives out, I apologise. I'm slowly losing it this morning. You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have another possibility, I mean, cutting short your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will take that to heart. Perhaps a long break.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told us that even after Mr. Borovcanin assumed his new duties with the special police brigade in 1994, you would see him when he visited his parents in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, after the encounter with him that you told us about, late in the day on 12 July, when was the next time you saw him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember when, but I probably did see him. I mean, I did see him around.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that you would see him with some regularity, certainly with the same regularity that you saw him in 1993 and 1994, when he was around visiting --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you understand my question, sir? Do I need to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you continue to see Mr. Borovcanin following July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When, sir, was the last time you were in contact, either directly or indirectly, with Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, can you give us a year?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you testified as a Defence witness on behalf of Colonel Blagojevic on the 17th of 18th of May, 2004. Other than my friends from Mr. Borovcanin's Defence team, what other representatives of other accused, either in this case or other cases, have you been in contact with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I only met with the representatives of Mr. Borovcanin and Defence counsel for Mr. Gvero.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thought I heard before Ms. Nikolic indicating that she had met you as well? Ms. Nikolic representing Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we just need an audible answer.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, that was two days ago here in The Hague at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps he can clarify whether he has met anyone else in recent days, in the last few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Will do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Have you understood His Honour's question, sir? Have you met anyone else from any other teams in the last few days?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Just one last question on this topic. How many times did you meet with the Defence team for Mr. Borovcanin, and if you can recall, when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to give you a number, but over the period of last five or six months, it may have been three, four, or five times, and then again in The Hague when they were preparing me for this testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to take you back a little bit. You were asked some questions in your examination in chief about your service to the Bratunac municipality, either in the capacity of Chief of Staff or later as commander of the staff of the TO to your duties in the brigade. I want to turn your attention to 1992 and 1993. That was a time, particularly in late 1992 into the winter and then spring of 1993, of significant military activity in your area of responsibility, was it not, sir? From late 1992 through the spring of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with some of the operations which were conducted by the VRS which included elements from the Bratunac Brigade? And let me just throw out a couple of names to you to see if you recognise them: Operation Proboj, meaning breakthrough, from November of 1992 to February of 1993. Do you remember that operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, not under that name at least. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I understand that you might not remember the particular code name. How about Operation Pesnica, Fist, from approximately mid-January to late January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with these names. There were operations, but the titles that you have just mentioned don't ring any bells, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. The operations, whatever their names were, included the liberation of Cerska, Konjevic Polje, and then eastward towards Srebrenica. Does that help you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those were the operations that were taking place during the first half of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall that as it happened on both sides of the conflict, as it were, the Muslim inhabitants of those communities and settlements because of these operations began to move into the Srebrenica area? Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What period are you referring to, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This period during which we have been speaking, these operations and -- to liberate Cerska, Konjevic Polje, do you recall that one of the effects of that was that the Muslim inhabitants of those communities, as Serbs did in other communities when their areas were attacked or taken over, fled towards the Srebrenica area and became refugees in the Srebrenica area; do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall when General Morillon went to Srebrenica in March of 1993, and then sometime after that, there were convoys of refugees from Srebrenica who clamored aboard to leave the enclave. Do you remember that happening, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall that during this entire period of time Mr. Borovcanin was the commander of the Bratunac police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to show you one document to help square away some dates that you've provided us on a couple of issues. In the Blagojevic case you testified that you were assistant commander for security and intelligence in August of 1992, and that was at the transcript 9319 from that case. Yesterday, and then again today, I think, your recollection was that it was September and October of that year. And you additionally testified that your recollection was that Mr. Borovcanin arrived in the Bratunac area in early 1993. I'd just like to show you one document, if I could, that's 65 ter 68 -- I'm sorry, 3813. What we have here, sir, is a report of a performance inspection at the Bratunac public security station. It was conducted on 22 and 23 August 1992. This document is dated the 27th of August, 1992. And it basically concerns -- what it says, an inspection by a supervisor of the SJB there in Zvornik, a supervisor named Sasa Blagojevic. What I want to turn your attention to, sir, is page 2 of the English, and that is page 2 of the B/C/S as well. And in your version, the original, there is a paragraph that begins: "After all these talks which were held at the Bratunac SJB, we agreed on a meeting with representatives of the army and the municipal government." Do you see that paragraph, sir, it's the third bullet point on your page? Just let me know if you're with me on this.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It says this meeting was attended by the president of the municipality, Mr. Ljubisav Simic; the chairman of the SDS, Miroslav --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We never challenged the fact when Mr. Borovcanin arrived. I mean, maybe I can help my friend by saying this that Mr. Borovcanin was at that period at the police station in Bratunac. We are not challenging the fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You need to take notice of that --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and proceed accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It also indicates that the chairman of the SDS, Miroslav Deronjic, and war commissioner, Zoran Tesic, on behalf of the municipality were present. It also indicates Colonel Dimitrije Sibinic, and that's the commander whom you told us about yesterday, correct, sir, under whom you served initially?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then it refers to staff sergeant Drago Nikolic on behalf of the army, head of SJB Luka Bogdanovic, and commander of the police station Ljubomir Borovcanin. And then there are two other names, Branimir Tesic and Budimir Lakicevic. My first question, sir, is: Does this jog your memory at all about when it was that you were serving in the intel and security organ? Do you recall attending this meeting or learning about the meeting that's described here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I was present at the meeting. I don't believe so, and it is not indicated in the document either.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, there is a reference to a staff sergeant Drago Nikolic on behalf of the army. Do you have any idea, sir, as to whether that Drago Nikolic referred to there, based on your service in the intel and security organ, as well as the familiarity that you told us about earlier in answer to my friend Madam Nikolic's questions with Drago Nikolic, whether this is the same Drago Nikolic who is the accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had known Drago Nikolic, and as far as this document is concerned and whether this is the same Drago Nikolic, I suppose that it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I'd like to move on. You were asked some questions yesterday about some orders regarding disconnecting the telephone lines in Bratunac during the Krivaja 95 operation. Do you remember those questions, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'd just like to show you two quick documents on that topic. The first is 65 ter 3817, please. And I apologise, we don't have an English translation of this document, but it's a very short one so I just have a couple of questions to put to you, sir. We can see it's dated the 5th of July, 1995. It's from the command of your brigade to PTT in Bratunac from your commander, Colonel Blagojevic. Can you just read what paragraph 1 says, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "Starting with the 5th of July, 1995, at 1200 hours, until further notice all post and telecommunication services users shall be excluded from the PTT system, and as for the private telephones, they have to be switched off even for the local use.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologizes for not being able to interpret the meaning of word l-o-k-a-l-u precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we need to know what it means, l-o ... yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, is there another way for you to define this word, "lokalu," l-o-k-a-l-u, that we see here in paragraph 1? Can you explain that to us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that private telephones cannot be used even in Bratunac. Local calls are also banned, meaning you cannot even call a fellow citizen in Bratunac. This is the meaning of the word.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If we go to paragraph 2, what is that -- that first line there say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brigade commander, 881-122.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, I apologise, sir. Can you read to us what the text is right after the number 2. Can you tell us what that says there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The following telephone numbers should not be switched off ..." Do you want me to go through them?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you would -- we don't need you to read us the telephone numbers, but if you could just read us what the abbreviations are there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under 2, it says: "The following telephone numbers should not be switched off: The brigade commander, president of the municipal assembly, the SDS," which stands for the Serbian Democratic Party, "the chief of the MUP," which stands for the chief of the Ministry of the Interior, "NOMO, the director of the PTT," which stands for the post, telegraph and telephone, "and the director -- the general manager of Vihor."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what is NOMO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: NOMO stands for the chief of the department of the ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in July 1995, who was chief of the MUP in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was Mr. Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you, sir. We're done with this document. Now, you told us yesterday -- and I want to turn your attention now to the planning stages of the Krivaja 95 operation. You told us yesterday that your brigade command reviewed and discussed both the warning order as well as the plan for active combat operations which were issued by the corps, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I believe you testified yesterday, and if I showed you your brigade's book of reports and meetings, the 5 July combat order was actually read out to the command staff. And you can confirm that, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, can we agree, sir, that you were in fact duty-bound to study that 2 July Drina Corps command combat order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have that connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, in --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise to my colleagues --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- that he should just pay attention. "I did have that connection," that's the answer which was recorded and I think if --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. I was just going to follow up on whether that was ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And I believe it would be maybe useful for the witness to have in front of him the document that my colleagues is referring at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President. I can call up the report and meetings book if -- can we have P219, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for the English, sir, on your screen do you see the cover of a book with which you are familiar, the book of reports and meetings for the brigade? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if we go to page 9 of the English, and that's also page 9 of the B/C/S, I think you just agreed with me, but I'll show you the document in any event. Do you see where it says -- actually, we need to go to page 10 of both documents. At the top, at 1930 hours, which has been incorrectly, I think, translated in the English as 0730 hours, but do you see where it says: "1930 hours, the brigade commander presented the order of the Drina Corps command to the command"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that's what we were just talking about, right, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see we are coming up on a break. I have some more involved documents to use with the witness. Is it okay to take it a couple of minutes early?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I have a meeting --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have a meeting now at 10.30, so I suggest that the break will be of 30 minutes instead of 25, and it will give you time -- also an opportunity to recover your voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Thayer, let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I just wanted to follow up with you. A question that I had for you that gave rise to the intervention from my friend was with respect to the Krivaja 95 combat order from the corps. You were duty-bound to review that, were you not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just as a matter of clarification, can you tell us the difference between the commander and the chief within an SJB?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I did not understand your question. What is the difference between ...

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Sometimes we see the term "commander," other times we see "chief" referred to. Are you familiar with the differences in the positions within an SJB?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really apologise. Commander of security -- security commander? I really did not understand you. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think we're having -- we may be having some translation issues?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not sure of that as yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just want to make sure --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Within -- I'll just move on, Mr. President. It's just a point of clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were asked some questions yesterday by my friend Mr. Zivanovic, on behalf of Colonel Popovic, about the Krivaja 95 plan from the corps and what was done at the brigade level to implement that combat order. Do you remember those questions, sir? There were some notations on the Bratunac Brigade's copy of the Drina Corps order for active combat operations. Do you remember those questions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, turning your attention to the questions concerning Momir Nikolic's notations on the Bratunac Brigade copy that you saw yesterday, and to save time I'll just refer to the documents. If you need to see them, I can certainly show them to you, but I think we can carry on with just a discussion about them. Can we agree that the notations that were made by yourself, as well as Mr. Nikolic, were not really corrections. They were notations to yourselves in implementing the task set by your superior command.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were corrections and changes that would be entered into the text of the order of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And those changes were made as you and the other staff members were deciding how best to implement the intent of that combat order, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's just to specify. Could my colleague specify what he means by "staff members"? When he says "staff," what are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it brigade staff or something else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm referring to, for example, yourself and Mr. Nikolic. You being a member of the command staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] President, I think this has to be clarified. I don't think the witness was a member of the military staff. He was a member of the command of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer. Thank you, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, as chief of logistics, I'm just trying to keep it simple, when you received that order, you made notations on that copy, as did Mr. Nikolic, in the course of deciding how best to implement the intent of your superior command in drafting the brigade's corresponding combat order, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I made these corrections in the sense that the infantry weapons' ammunition should be taken only to our units that are in active combat, and that is for the Bratunac Brigade and only the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And it should go without saying, sir, shouldn't it, that you wouldn't be making changes that would violate or override what you thought the intent of your superior command's order was. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, based on your experience in your brigade, it's the military police who are responsible for dealing with prisoners of war, that is, guarding them, escorting them, for example, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you don't have any reason to believe that that common practice was changed in the case of the Bratunac Brigade combat order, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you don't have any reason to believe that the common practice, the understood role of the military police, as you just told us, involved guarding and escorting prisoners of war, you don't have any reason to believe that that was changed for any reason in the Bratunac Brigade combat order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to turn your attention to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, may we know any reference to common practice as by Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't understand. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Maybe it's my mistake but I don't follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. May we have any reference to common practice regarding the duties of military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I get you now. Do you have any reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My reference, sir, is his answer to -- Mr. President, is his answer to my question at line 22 of page 31, asking whether in his experience in the brigade, it was the military police who were responsible for dealing with prisoners of war. He understood my question and he answered it clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. I think you can proceed. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to take you back to your visit to the forward command post at Pribicevac. You were asked some questions by my learned friend representing General Gvero. I want to just read to you what you said in the Blagojevic trial about your time with General Gvero. And this is at page 9435 of the transcript. You were asked the question: "Do you recall seeing anyone, any higher echelon officers from the corps or from the Main Staff?" And your answer was: "General Gvero from the Main Staff of the VRS was there, and I went to see General Gvero together with Mr. Davidovic. We had a coffee or some drinks, I can't remember exactly. And we talked for a while about the current problems." You were asked a follow-up question: "What were the current problems that you talked about?" And your answer was: "Well, you know, the activities that were being carried out around Srebrenica." Now, this conversation occurred on 9 July, while the combat activities were still ongoing. So it's correct, sir, is it not, that when you referred there in Blagojevic to the activities going on, you are referring to -- naturally talking about the military activities that were underway at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I want to turn your attention to another area, the materiel supplies during the Krivaja 95 operation. I first want to clarify a couple of details with you, and then we are going to look at some records. You had a rear service or logistics company of approximately 20 men, and that was commanded by Captain Radosavljevic; is that correct, sir? Are you not receiving interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I don't think the witness is receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: He's looking at me --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's what he's saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Will you repeat your question, please. Maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think we may need to find out exactly when we lost it because he's been giving me a funny look for a little while, which I thought was just me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us when you stopped receiving interpretation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just repeat the question because the previous question he had answered yes. So it's only your last question. Just come and read it out again.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you had a rear service logistics company of about 20 men captained -- commanded by Captain Radosavljevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you still not receiving interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes, I am receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. Okay. Then you can, perhaps, answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The logistics platoon company -- captain, the commander of the logistics platoon was Captain Milos Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where was your officer physically located?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My office was at the same place as the brigade command, at the building of the former tile factory called Kaolin.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just to follow up on a couple of questions, you testified that fuel would be taken by the brigade from the Vihor company's gas station, but you also had the capacity to store your own fuel at the brigade warehouse. And can you confirm that you stored that fuel in barrels, that you had a capacity of storing up to a tonne to a tonne and a half of fuel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are capacities that apply to the fuel stored in metal barrels, up to 200 litres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you talked about a couple of warehouses yesterday. Do you know where the MUP stored its materiel? They certainly had a warehouse somewhere in Bratunac for its logistic needs. Do you know what that location was, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably in the compound of the police station building.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you were shown yesterday your 3 July request for equipment and materiel to the Drina Corps command. And to save time, I don't need to go through it with you, but can you confirm that you recall that request that you put to the corps command upon receiving the warning order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn your attention now to the actual - and I'll just use your abbreviation MTS - the materiel and technical equipment that you did receive during the Krivaja 95 operation. May we have 65 ter 3812, please. Do you remember giving a statement, sir, to the MUP in August of 2003 at the Bratunac police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember giving a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you see a copy of it before us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 of the B/C/S, and that's page 4 of the English. I wanted to ask you about something you said during this interview. Referring to the Srebrenica operation in July 95 you stated, and I quote: "The supply of units with combat and non-combat materiel and technical equipment was carried out directly through the Main Staff and the logistics of the corps." We have to -- do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please help me?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sure, it's in about the middle of that paragraph. You're talking about Operation Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What I want to ask you, sir, is can you explain to the Trial Chamber how the Main Staff and the corps logistics organs interacted to supply your brigade during the Krivaja 95 operation? And we're done with the document. For example, what elements of the Main Staff were working with the corps to accomplish the task?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the logistics organs of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who were the personnel that you were familiar with during this period of time at the Main Staff logistics -- in the Main Staff logistics organ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the technical service, for example, it was Lieutenant-Colonel or Colonel Cvijetic [phoen]. I would need to think about it now. I can't remember exactly all the senior officers that -- well, I mostly had contacts with senior officers from the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Understood, sir, but when you talk about the Main Staff or working directly with the Main Staff in the corps logistics, can you explain what that process was during the Krivaja 95 operation? How did they interact? Can you just tell the Court how those two echelons worked together during the operation, based on your recollection and experience?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really tell you about the cooperation between the Main Staff and the corps organs. As I said, mostly all the activities that related to the brigade went through the logistics sector of the corps, the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's look at some documents. If we could have 65 ter 3818 on e-court, please. Now, sir, with Madam Usher's help, I'm going to show you some documents that I think you've seen before.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The copies in e-court are pretty hard to read so I have the originals here, and if we could just keep them in order, and maybe it would be best to put them on the ELMO, if we could. Just one at a time take them out of the plastic and put them on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday materiel lists, and we can see in the upper left-hand corner that it says "materielni [phoen] list." Is this an example of what you were talking about, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's the materiel list, materielni list.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. This is dated the 5th of July, and --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- if we look at box four, it says "VP 7111." Am I correct that that's the military post number for the Drina Corps command in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't remember the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, next to that it says: "H. Pijesak." That, I presume, stands for Han Pijesak, right in that same box next to VP 7111, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the Main Staff is located there, correct, in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We can see that this is a materiel list for various sizes of ammunition ranging from 7.62 millimetre, all the way up to 105 millimetre, which I presume is a howitzer. Do you agree, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, 105 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you know whether the materiel in this document was delivered in response to your 3 July request that we spoke about before; or would there have been a separate request that was made by the brigade which led to this materiel list and this ammunition being delivered?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to look at my request to the corps; for example, here I have 30-millimetre bullet, that is item 5. And as far as I can remember, we didn't have that kind of materiel.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to the next document, if we could, please, and that's 65 ter 3819. And this will be a 6 July, 1995, materiel list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Try now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not about an objection, but I just clarify a point because on the document we have still in front of us 711, 11, this is the military post of what? After that we speak about the staff. Could the witness clarify where was the logistic bases of the Drina Corps, so that we would know what it's all about in this document. Because this military number 711, we would like to know what it is exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The depots could have been in different positions which largely depended on the MTS which was stored in them. As for this document, we can see that the Tisca depot is where the ammunition was. And as for Han Kram in Han Pijesak, that's where the quartermaster supplies were stored; in other words, we are not talking about just one depot or storage.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, the corps, as well as the Main Staff, had their own logistics centres or depots, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you remember that one of the Main Staff depots was known as the 35th. You recall that, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, let's look at another document, sir. Let's go to, if we can have 3819. Sir, this is another materiel list dated 7 July, and for the record, we are looking at ERN 0663540. This is 3820, 65 ter 3820. Again, do you see that there is ammunition being delivered in this materiel list, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could scroll -- sorry. If we could just maybe move the original to the bottom. A little bit more, that's great.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you see box 36, sir? There is a handwritten notation in the lower right-hand corner. Do you see where it says that the listed materiel came directly from the 35 POB? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So this is coming directly from the Main Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- depot?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness -- can the witness see the top of the document with the name of the person who sent this equipment, or what is the origin of this materiel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Can we do that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know if that helps you at all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- seeing the top of the document. But my question is really focused on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, one moment, Mr. Thayer. Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure if there is a translation in English of this document, but if my colleague doesn't really know the contents of the document, in this case I don't think he can allege things which are simply not true. On this document, one can read the data concerning the sender, and then you have the number of the military post, 7111, and then the place, Vlasenica. So maybe the witness can clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I do not assume, like Ms. Fauveau, that you do not know the contents of this document; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You are correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you can proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Turning your attention to the bottom of the document -- sorry, Madam Usher. Do you see, sir is, where it says that the listed materiel came directly from the 35 POB? That's at the lower right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that indicates, does it not, sir, that this materiel came directly from that Main Staff logistics centre?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, Mr. President, because this document shows clearly who sent this materiel. And on this document you can see the military post 7111, Vlasenica, as the sender.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can proceed. I mean, the question is perfectly legitimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, let me try a third time. That handwritten annotation down there in the box indicates, does it not, that this listed materiel came directly from the Main Staff's logistics centre of the 35th POB logistics centre. Isn't that what it says in black and white, or blue and white?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my colleague continues to say and persists that it comes directly from the staff. I don't say that it doesn't come from the 35th bases but not from the staff, it's not on the document. There is also the name of the person who signed the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question is eliciting from the witness precisely the source of this document. So he is in a position -- if he is in a position to answer, he will answer, especially since he has heard what you have to say now. Yes, please, Mr. Trisic, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The supplies came directly from the 31st -- 35th logistics base. There is the document in front of us indicating that, and there is no way I can deny it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, to save some time, I'm going to again ask the help of Madam Usher. I just want to hand you a packet of some more original materiel lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And for the record, this contains 65 ter 3821, 3823, 3824, and 32825. And if you would just, Madam Usher, just give a packet to the witness so he can just go through them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I just ask you to look at those one by one, and I would just ask you to, when you're done looking at them, confirm that those are all materiel lists for ammunition received during the Krivaja 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Obviously the ammunition was received during the Krivaja operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. We're done with that packet, then. Now, you were shown yesterday, and again let me know if you need it, but you were shown a document that was dated Petrovdan 1995, regarding the consumption of MTS from 10 July to 12 July that you sent to the Drina Corps command. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. You also said that that didn't necessarily mean that you had used all that materiel, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, in the Blagojevic case, you testified that you would not receive any accounting or receipt from the subordinate command of how the materiel was used, and that was at page 9324. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now in your interview with the OTP, at pages 26 and 27, you said that in relation to that consumption document, and I quote: "An operations man in the unit would know how much was actually used." And you continue that: "The operations organs were ones who take control of how much each unit used of ammunition because operations organs know which unit was involved in the operations." Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you just tell the Trial Chamber briefly when you would make your assessments of the brigades needs, would you have to rely on the operations organ, therefore, in order to properly assess the needs and make the required requests, or would you rely on some other method of doing that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you have just said it, that would be the right order of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. You were asked some questions this morning about fuel that was consumed and received on the -- on the 13th of July. I want to ask you some questions related to that topic. May we have 65 ter 3827, please. And with Madam Usher's help, I am going to hand you some originals. This is a packet of fuel-related materiel lists I am handing out to you. Now, sir, can you look at the first two. Those are -- and then I'll ask you about the document that is on the screen. The first two documents there are dated July 8th and 10th of 1995, for 800 and 400 litres respectively. And for the record this is 65 ter 3826 and 3822. Do you see those two documents? Those are the two documents I am referring to, sir, for 800 and 400 litres?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have any recollection of what that -- those fuel deliveries were for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe for the activities of the brigade. I can't be more specific. These are very low quantities, 400 litres, 600 litres. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. If you just put those two documents to the side, then, and let's turn our attention to the document that's on the screen, and that will be the next original. If you would just look at the next original in that packet after those first two ones that I gave you, because the e-court version, as you can see, is illegible. So if you can pull those two top documents and put them to the side, and then the next document, if you could put that next to you on the ELMO, we will be able to see more clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We're going to need your assistance, again, Madam. If we can just put that document that Mr. Trisic has in his hand on the ELMO, I think we will be able to read it a little easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: As we can see, this is a materiel list for July 12th, 1995, showing 5.000 litres of D-2 diesel fuel being delivered. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, that's a substantial amount of fuel, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could go to 3828, and that's going to be the next document in your stack there, sir. If we can put that next document on the ELMO. We're done with that one. Again, this is another materiel list dated 12 July for 2.000 litres of diesel fuel, D-2. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But you have misspoken, it doesn't say "we request" but "we have received."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Understood, understood, sir. This is fuel that -- that is coming to you that you were receiving. And on that note, when you say that this isn't fuel that you requested, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, given the date, the 12th of July, this fuel could only have been used for the buses that transported the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. And if we could go to the next document in your pile, put that on the ELMO, and this is 65 ter 3829, we see that there is 6.000 litres of diesel fuel, D-2, being delivered to your brigade that day.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you were shown --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher, I think we're actual done with this packet now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
